# crit_val_op {#sec-doc}


::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="docblock" collapse=false}


```julia
crit_val_op(chart_choice, m, n_patterns; alpha=0.05)
```
Compute the asymptotic critical value of the ordinal-pattern test [`test_op`](test_op.qmd).
 
The critical value depends only on the chart, on the pattern length `m`, on the number of patterns `n_patterns` and on the level `alpha`, but not on the data. In a Monte Carlo study it can therefore be computed once per sample size and reused in every replication, which is much faster than calling [`test_op`](test_op.qmd) in the loop: [`test_op`](test_op.qmd) additionally evaluates the p-value, and for [`Shannon()`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.Shannon), [`ShannonExtropy()`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.ShannonExtropy) and [`DistanceToWhiteNoise()`](DistanceToWhiteNoise.qmd) that means a numerical evaluation of a generalized chi-squared distribution per call.
 
  * `chart_choice`: one of [`Shannon()`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.Shannon), [`ShannonExtropy()`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.ShannonExtropy), [`DistanceToWhiteNoise()`](DistanceToWhiteNoise.qmd), [`UpDownBalance()`](UpDownBalance.qmd), [`Persistence()`](Persistence.qmd), [`RotationalAsymmetry()`](RotationalAsymmetry.qmd), [`UpDownScaling()`](UpDownScaling.qmd). For [`Shannon`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.Shannon) and [`ShannonExtropy`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.ShannonExtropy), the statistic is in the logarithm base of the chart, which must be larger than 1. Both default to base 2 in ComplexityMeasures.jl; use [`Shannon(base=exp(1))`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.Shannon) for the natural logarithm used in the papers. Statistic and critical value are both in that base, so the test decision and the p-value do not depend on it.
  * `m::Int`: length of the ordinal patterns. Asymptotic theory is available for `m = 3` (and `m = 2` for [`Shannon()`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.Shannon), [`DistanceToWhiteNoise()`](DistanceToWhiteNoise.qmd) and [`UpDownBalance()`](UpDownBalance.qmd)).
  * `n_patterns::Int`: number of ordinal patterns, `length(ts) - (m - 1) * d`.
  * `alpha=0.05`: significance level.
The null hypothesis is rejected when the statistic falls below the critical value for [`Shannon()`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.Shannon) and [`ShannonExtropy()`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.ShannonExtropy), exceeds it for [`DistanceToWhiteNoise()`](DistanceToWhiteNoise.qmd), and exceeds it in absolute value for the four statistics of Bandt (2019).
 

```julia
x = randn(500)
n = length(x) - 2
crit = crit_val_op(Persistence(), 3, n)
abs(chart_stat_op(stat_op(x; chart_choice=Persistence())[2], Persistence())) > crit
```


:::
